overview: City officials and consultants presented proposed rezoning plans for Medford Square to the public, focusing on new mixed-use districts, height incentives for community benefits, and environmental standards. The meeting featured a presentation on proposed dimensional changes followed by a question-and-answer session regarding traffic, parking, and neighborhood character.

items.title: Zoning Process and Project Scope
items.summary: Councilor Matt Leming and staff introduced the project team and explained that the proposed zoning changes are a collaborative effort between the City Council and the Community Development Board to implement the 2023 Comprehensive Plan.

items.title: Presentation on Proposed Medford Square Zoning
items.summary: Consultant Emily Innes outlined the shift from use-based separation to mixed-use districts (1B, 2A, 2B, and 3) intended to increase housing density and support local businesses. The proposal includes a 'base height' allowed by right and an 'incentive height' granted in exchange for community benefits like affordable housing or energy efficiency.

items.title: Dimensional and Environmental Standards
items.summary: The presentation detailed new standards for active ground floors, pervious surfaces, and a 'Green Score' system to improve stormwater management and public health. Innes noted that parking requirements are being revised to provide more flexibility based on recent public feedback.

items.title: Public Q&A: Land Use and Traffic
items.summary: Staff clarified that the Salem Street substation is owned by National Grid and explained that traffic modeling is conducted during individual site plan reviews rather than as part of the general rezoning process.

items.title: Public Q&A: Density and Neighborhood Character
items.summary: Residents expressed concerns about 15-story building heights; staff responded that the proposal actually lowers current maximum height limits and requires height step-backs to protect adjacent residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Public Q&A: Parking, Solar Rights, and Infrastructure
items.summary: Public commenters argued that new developments lack sufficient parking and that increased heights might impede solar rights for existing homes. Councilor Leming noted that while zoning impacts future development, broader traffic issues at the I-93 rotary require state-level intervention.
